evals.name: airtable-source-with-pill-conflict
evals.prompt: I've got a design system spec for Airtable's marketing site at references/design-systems/DESIGN-airtable.md inside the tenant folder. Add it as a new theme for my iSemantics content so I can use it for LinkedIn infographics.
evals.expected_output: New THEMES.md section covering all 14 catalog elements, family chrome added (tag pill, watermark, body field, author footer, Lucide, 24px floor), the pill-radius conflict resolved and logged as a documented deviation, registered in the comparison table + usage rules + README, and a rendered reference asset that passes validation.
assertions: New theme section in THEMES.md defines all 14 catalog elements (page/canvas, atmosphere, tags/pills, headline, feature cards, hero card, info grid, icons, stat bars, stat numbers, takeaway, step/timeline, SVG illustrations, footer)
Tag pill is specified as a pill (radius 9999px or 50px), positioned as first child top-left
Background watermark type is specified with a colour and opacity
Author footer is specified (photo, name, role, logo, domain)
No type size below 24px appears in the theme spec
Registered in all four places: THEMES.md section, quick comparison table column, usage rules, README theme list
Source DESIGN-*.md left byte-identical to the original
A reference asset PNG exists on disk
Reference asset passes both the pre-render and post-render validators
Conflicts between the source's rules and tenant chrome are logged under a Documented deviations heading
Pill-radius conflict (source reserves pill for pricing) is explicitly addressed

evals.name: figma-source-with-viewport-rule
evals.prompt: Same exercise with this one: references/design-systems/DESIGN-figma.md in the tenant folder. Convert it into a theme I can use.
evals.expected_output: New THEMES.md section covering all 14 elements, the one-colour-block-per-viewport rule recognised and translated for a fixed 1080x1350 canvas, magenta's sub-4.5:1 contrast measured and written in as a rule, family chrome added, fully registered, reference asset rendered and validated.
